L13@P1: [Abstract] The distribution of prime numbers is a cornerstone of mathematics, yet its underlying
L14@P1: origin remains one of science's deepest mysteries. While probabilistic models successfully
L15@P1: describe the asymptotic density of primes, they inherently fail to explain the arithmetic rigidities
L16@P1: and short-range correlations that define the sequence. Here we show that prime statistics emerge
L17@P1: naturally from a low-dimensional deterministic physical system. By modeling the prime sieve as
L18@P1: a non-autonomous chaotic process subject to dissipation, we identify a topological isomorphism
L19@P1: between the arithmetic constraints of primes and the symbolic dynamics of the Logistic map at the
L20@P1: band-merging point. Our model quantitatively reproduces the Twin Prime Constant (C2≈0.6602)
L21@P1: with high precision, governed by a decay exponent strictly constrained by number-theoretic
L22@P1: axioms. This finding suggests that arithmetic randomness is not a form of noise, but a signature of
L23@P1: weak chaos, offering a unified physical framework that bridges the discrete world of number
L24@P1: theory and the continuous world of nonlinear dynamics.
L25@P1: Main
L26@P1: The distribution of prime numbers presents a fundamental duality that has puzzled mathematicians
L27@P1: for centuries: macroscopic randomness versus microscopic arithmetic rigidity. Since Riemann, the
L28@P1: dominant paradigm has treated the sequence of primes as a pseudo-random process. Traditional
L29@P1: probabilistic approaches, most notably the CramÈr model, successfully approximate the global
L30@P1: asymptotic density of primes but inherently fail to capture local deterministic constraints, such as
L31@P1: the strict prohibition of odd gaps (except for the first pair) and the short-range correlations induced
L32@P1: by modular arithmetic [1, 3]. This "coin-tossing" perspective creates a deep explanatory gap: it
L33@P1: can predict how many primes exist, but it cannot explain the precise topological structure of where
L34@P1: they appear.
L35@P1: To resolve this paradox, we propose a paradigm shift: modeling the prime sequence not as a
L36@P1: stochastic process, but as the trajectory of a low-dimensional deterministic chaotic system. We
L37@P1: posit that the unpredictability of primes is not due to high-dimensional noise, but is a signature of
L38@P1: deterministic chaos emerging from a simple nonlinear feedback loop. Specifically, we construct a
L39@P1-2: physical framework based on the non-autonomous Logistic map operating at the Band-Merging Point (uc≈1.5437). In this view, the Sieve of Eratosthenes is reformulated as a dynamic wave
L40@P2: interference process, where the "aging" of the system (parameter decay) corresponds to the
L41@P2: thinning density of primes, while the chaotic attractor provides the rigid topological skeleton.
L42@P2: This approach unifies the topological structure of chaos with the asymptotic sparsity of number
L43@P2: theory [4]. Unlike purely stochastic models, our framework demonstrates that the "randomness"
L44@P2: of primes is effectively a specific universality class of weak chaos. By decoupling the microscopic
L45@P2: structure (determined by the chaotic attractor) from the macroscopic density (determined by the
L46@P2: aging mechanism), our model successfully reproduces key statistical fingerprints of primes that
L47@P2: have long eluded probabilistic explanations—most notably, the precise quantization of the Twin
L48@P2: Prime Constant.
L49@P2: Model Construction: From Dynamic Sieves to Continuous Chaos

L51@P2: bridging arithmetic sieves and nonlinear dynamics. Our approach follows a three-stage progression:
L52@P2: transforming the static sieving process into a dynamic symbol sequence, mapping this sequence to
L53@P2: the orbit of a low-dimensional chaotic attractor via symbolic dynamics, and finally, introducing a
L54@P2: non-autonomous aging mechanism to reconcile the model with the asymptotic sparsity of primes
L55@P2: (Fig. 1).

L82@P3: we reformulate the classical Sieve of Eratosthenes not merely as a static elimination algorithm, but
L83@P3: as a dynamical system evolving in time. In this physical picture, the natural number line is
L84@P3: conceptualized as a medium propagating signal waves. With the introduction of the first modulo2 sieve, the axis bifurcates into a "retained" state (corresponding to potential primes) and an
L85@P3: "eliminated" state (corresponding to composites), manifesting as a simple periodic waveform.
L86@P3: However, as subsequent sieves (modulo-3, modulo-5, etc.) are continuously superimposed, these
L87@P3: oscillations with incommensurate frequencies undergo nonlinear interference. This interference
L88@P3: rapidly breaks the initial periodicity, evolving the system into a highly complex, aperiodic symbol
L89@P3: sequence.

L93@P3: the sequence topologically forbids consecutive "retained" states, directly corresponding to the
L94@P3: number-theoretic fact that the prime gap cannot be 1. From the perspective of dynamical systems
L95@P3: theory, these symbol sequences encode the system's coarse-grained trajectory in phase space,
L96@P3: containing full information about its underlying topological structure.

L226@P8: Discussion
L227@P8: In the intersection of number theory and statistical physics, the debate regarding the origin of
L228@P8: randomness in prime distribution has persisted for over a century [1,3]. However, the dominant
L229@P8-9: paradigm—exemplified by the CramÈr model—remains largely confined to describing the macroscopic asymptotic density of primes. While recent advances in Quantum Chaos have
L230@P9: revealed striking statistical isomorphisms between Riemann zeros and the GUE ensemble [9],
L231@P9: these findings are primarily descriptive rather than generative: we observe that primes resemble
L232@P9: chaos, yet we lack the dynamical equations to generate them. Furthermore, existing chaotic models
L233@P9: are predominantly autonomous, possessing invariant measures that fundamentally contradict the
L234@P9: non-stationary nature of prime density, which exhibits asymptotic sparsity.
L235@P9: The decoupling of microscopic topology from macroscopic density is pivotal to understanding
L236@P9: prime distribution. Evaluating the validity of a dynamical model demands criteria distinct from
L237@P9: traditional curve fitting. Although previous studies have attempted to approximate the primecounting function by parameter tuning, these strategies often lack mechanistic explanatory power.
L238@P9: Since the prime sequence exhibits both high Arithmetic Rigidity (e.g., modular structures) and
L239@P9: macroscopic stochastic decay, no universal dynamical framework has yet succeeded in capturing
L240@P9: these orthogonal behaviors within a single system.
L241@P9: The central thesis of this paper is that a physical model of prime distribution can be rigorously
L242@P9: constructed based on a Non-Autonomous Chaotic System. A defining feature of non-autonomous
L243@P9: systems is that their control parameters evolve temporally, allowing the system to modify its phase
L244@P9: space measure while preserving its topological structure. Crucially, the microscopic structure of
L245@P9: primes (such as forbidden gaps) is determined by the system's Topological Skeleton, independent
L246@P9: of specific evolution times; conversely, macroscopic density is strictly dependent on the passage
L247@P9: of time (magnitude). Therefore, the solution lies in a mechanism that couples a stable chaotic
L248@P9: attractor with a dynamic "aging" process. The "Shrinking Target" mechanism proposed here
L249@P9: implements precisely this physical strategy: the nonlinear folding of the Logistic map near the
L250@P9: Band-Merging Point provides a deterministic microscopic skeleton, while the time-decaying
L251@P9: parameter u(n) acts as a dissipation term, guiding the trajectory toward gradual sparsification while
L252@P9: maintaining ergodicity.
L253@P9: Our results demonstrate that this dynamical framework possesses predictive power beyond mere
L254@P9: numerical simulation. If the system were a simple random walk, the precise convergence of the
L255@P9: Twin Prime Constant C2
L256@P9:  to 0.6602 would be inexplicable. By reformulating the twin prime
L257@P9: problem as a Recurrence Problem in a non-autonomous dynamical system, we identify that C2
L258@P9: effectively serves as a "coupling constant" between the chaotic mixing rate and the density decay
L259@P9: rate. This quantitative consistency (error <10
L260@P9: −4) strongly suggests that the prime sequence belongs
L261@P9: to a specific Universality Class of "Weak Chaos", defined jointly by a positive Lyapunov
L262@P9-10: exponent and specific scaling laws. This offers a novel physical perspective on the Hardy-Littlewood conjecture: the emergence of arithmetic progressions is not a purely probabilistic
L263@P10: coincidence, but an inevitable outcome of deterministic chaos in a dissipative environment.
L264@P10: Our framework can be generalized to elucidate number-theoretic phenomena beyond twin primes.
L265@P10: For instance, Polignac's Conjecture (prime pairs with gap 2k) can be analyzed by adjusting the
L266@P10: geometry of the Target Window in phase space. For systems involving additive structures like
L267@P10: the Goldbach Conjecture, the framework could be extended to Coupled Map Lattices (CML),
L268@P10: where synchronization or anti-synchronization states of chaotic oscillators might correspond to
L269@P10: specific additive decompositions. Furthermore, this "Aging Chaos" model may offer insights into
L270@P10: other complex physical systems exhibiting asymptotic sparsification, such as relaxation processes
L271@P10: in glassy dynamics.
L272@P10: Currently, constructing a rigorous mathematical theory for such non-linear dynamic networks
L273@P10: remains a frontier challenge. The difficulty arises because classical Ergodic Theory is not directly
L274@P10: applicable to non-autonomous systems. Although our numerical experiments indicate that the
L275@P10: system is ergodic in an asymptotic sense and satisfies the dynamical form of the Borel-Cantelli
L276@P10: lemma, strictly proving that the "aging" trajectory of the Logistic map necessarily traverses all
L277@P10: admissible arithmetic patterns requires the development of new mathematical tools. Moreover,
L278@P10: given the extreme parameter sensitivity of prime distribution, distinguishing between numerical
L279@P10: computation errors and theoretical prediction deviations remains a critical focus for future research.
L280@P10: Resolving these issues will ultimately allow us to establish a unified physical framework,
L281@P10: fundamentally revealing the dynamical origin of arithmetic randomness.
